title: Architecture
text: Architecture Every project forja generates is hexagonal, also called ports and adapters. There is one rule behind it: dependencies point towards the domain. The business rules know nothing about the web framework, the database or the mail provider, and those pieces plug in from the outside. The layers Layer What it holds Node: packages/core/src/ Java: apps/api/.../<module / Domain entities, value objects, events, the rules domain/ domain/ Application use cases, one per class application/<module / application/ Ports the interfaces the use cases need ports/ application/port/ Infrastructure adapters and the composition root infrastructure/ infrastructure/ On Node, the hexagon is the packages/core workspace, shared by the web and mobile apps. On Java, each module of apps/api is its own small hexagon ( tasks to start with), plus a shared package for the cross cutting pieces such as DomainException and the CurrentUser port. Domain Plain TypeScript or plain Java: no framework, no database, no HTTP. An entity is created through a factory, such as User.create or Task.create . Value objects such as Email , Password and TaskTitle refuse invalid input when they are built, so the rest of the code can trust them. Application A use case orchestrates the domain through ports. Everything it needs from the outside world, such as a repository, a clock, a password hasher or a mailer, comes in through its constructor as an interface. That is what lets the tests run a use case against in memory adapters, with nothing started. On Java, use cases carry no framework annotations. CompleteTask is a plain final class with a constructor. Infrastructure Adapters implement the ports: Drizzle and in memory repositories, bcrypt, a console mailer, a system clock on Node; JDBC and in memory repositories, REST controllers, JWT security on Java. The infrastructure is also where the pieces are put together. The composition root One place knows both the use cases and the adapters, and wires them. On Node

title: Architecture
text: One place knows both the use cases and the adapters, and wires them. On Node it is packages/core/src/infrastructure/config/container.ts . buildContainer() creates the adapters and returns an object with every use case built on them. Each adapter is chosen by its own switch: hasDatabase() picks the Drizzle repositories when DATABASE URL is set and the in memory ones otherwise. There is no single "demo mode" flag that turns everything off at once. The container is kept on globalThis , so Next.js's separate server bundles share one instance and one set of in memory data. title: Architecture
section: What npm run arch and forja doctor check on Node
text: Node has no ArchUnit, so the generated project carries scripts/check architecture.mjs , run with npm run arch , and forja doctor runs the same check. The script has no dependencies, so it runs wherever the project does, and Specgate's gate runs it as arch cmd . Both check the core's imports. It reads every .ts and .tsx file under packages/core/src and fails when: any file imports next , react , react dom , react native or expo , or a subpath of them; a file in domain/ , application/ or ports/ imports from infrastructure/ . It names the file and the line, and suggests moving that code to apps/

title: Architecture
text: On Node, a use case returns a Result for the errors the business expects: RegisterUseCase returns err(new EmailAlreadyInUseError()) when the email is taken, and ok({ userId }) when it is not. The reasons: The signature says what can go wrong. Result<RegisterOutput, EmailAlreadyInUseError tells the caller which errors to handle; a thrown exception does not appear in the type. The caller has to look at ok before it can reach value , so an expected failure cannot slip through unhandled. title: Architecture
text: Most tests replace pieces with doubles. Java projects also get StartupTest , which starts the application with its real pieces. It proves that the real adapters exist and are wired, which a suite of green unit tests cannot.

title: CLI reference
text: CLI reference forja <command help prints the options of each command. forja init Creates a new project in ./<name . With no options it runs the wizard; with yes or config it asks nothing. Option Values Notes [name] lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter Required with yes . Also names the folder, the scope @<name and the default Java package. backend <backend node , spring , quarkus Default node . Picks the set of defaults with yes ; with config , replaces the file's. Any other value stops with Unknown backend . java package <pkg e.g. com.acme.shop Java only. Default com.<name without hyphens. archunit / no archunit Java only. ArchUnit is on by default for Java. Ignored on Node. platforms <list web , mobile , comma separated Node default web,mobile . Java: web , or "" for an API only. db <db postgres docker , none Default postgres docker . auth <auth sessions (Node), oauth2 (Java), none Node default sessions , Java default oauth2 . mailer <mailer console Used by Node sessions for password reset emails. design <design tailwind , none Default tailwind . tests <list unit , integration , e2e web Default unit,integration . The list replaces the default. extras <list lint , ci , docker , specgate Node default lint ; Java default lint,docker,specgate . The list replaces the default. pm <pm npm , pnpm , bun Default npm . Java backends use npm only. yes Ask nothing: the defaults plus the flags. config <path a forja.config.json Start from that file; the name and the flags override it. See [Configuration](config.md). dry run Print the file tree and write nothing. skip install Do not install the dependencies (and so do not adopt Specgate). skip git Do not run git init or make the first commit. What init does, in order 1. Builds the configuration from the wizard, from yes and the flags, or from config and the flags. 2. Validates it. An invalid configuration stops here, before anything is written. 3. Renders every file in memory, then formats .ts , .tsx , .j

title: Configuration
text: Configuration Every project forja creates has a forja.config.json at its root. It records the choices made at forja init , and forja add and forja doctor read it to know the backend, the package and the extras. You can also write one by hand, or copy one from another project, and pass it to forja init config . An example This is the file forja init shop yes backend spring writes: javaPackage only appears when you set it. $schema and version are written by forja and not read back. Fields Field Type Allowed values Required name string lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter yes scope string @ followed by lowercase letters, digits and hyphens yes platforms array web , mobile yes backend string node , spring , quarkus no, defaults to node javaPackage string dotted lowercase segments, at least two: com.acme.shop no archunit boolean true , false no, defaults to false arch string hexagonal yes db string postgres docker , none yes auth string sessions , oauth2 , none yes mailer string console yes design string tailwind , none yes ui string own yes edgeFunctions boolean false yes eas boolean false yes tests array unit , integration , e2e web yes extras array lint , ci , docker , specgate yes pm string npm , pnpm , bun (Java: npm only) yes arch , ui , edgeFunctions and eas have one accepted value today. They hold the place of options forja does not generate yet, and a hand written file must still include them. What each field means: scope names the internal packages: @shop/core , @shop/shared , @shop/web . platforms lists the apps. On Java, [] means an API only. backend decides where the logic lives: packages/core in TypeScript, or apps/api in Java. javaPackage is the root Java package. Without it, forja uses com.<name with the hyphens removed. archunit adds the ArchUnit test on Java. db: none keeps the in memory repositories; postgres docker adds PostgreSQL in Docker. auth: sessions is the built in session auth on Node; oauth2 is Keycloak and Auth.js on

title: Contributing
text: Contributing This page is for working on forja itself. You need Node.js 22 or newer. To check what forja generates for Java, you also need a JDK 21 and Docker. Set up Day to day Command What it does npm run dev <args runs the CLI from src/ with tsx, no build needed npm test the vitest suite in tests/ npm run test:watch the same, in watch mode npm run typecheck tsc noEmit npm run lint ESLint over src and tests npm run build compiles to dist/ , which the forja binary runs npm run site builds this documentation site from site/ into site/ , to look at locally npm run site:publish builds it into docs/ , which GitHub Pages serves from main : commit the result dry run is the quickest way to see what a change does: The tests cover the configuration rules ( schema.test.ts ), the recipe order ( planner.test.ts ), the rendering of every Java combination and of the Node path ( render.test.ts , render node.test.ts ), the end to end recipe ( e2e web.test.ts ), the next steps ( postinstall.test.ts ), forja add ( add.test.ts ) and forja doctor ( doctor.test.ts ). Proving a generated project works The unit tests show that forja renders the right files. scripts/verify generated.sh shows that those files work: it generates a project with the built CLI, installs it and runs everything. For each backend it runs forja init with Playwright and the extras, then forja add usecase , add entity and add port , forja doctor , the tests, the type check and lint. On Node it also builds the web app for production, bundles the mobile app for iOS, Android and web, and runs expo doctor . Then it runs the Playwright tests in a real browser, and last specgate validate strict . What it needs: Docker running. The Java paths start PostgreSQL and Keycloak with docker compose up d wait , and Testcontainers or Dev Services start their own PostgreSQL. Ports 3000, 5432, 8080 and 8180 free. title: Contributing
text: A recipe is one concern of the generated project. It lives in src/recipes/<id .ts , and its templates in templates/<id / . apply receives a RecipeContext . Everything it writes goes to an in memory file system; nothing reaches the disk until every recipe has run and Prettier has formatted the result. Method What it does ctx.config the validated configuration ctx.has(flag) whether flag is in platforms , tests or extras ctx.copyFile(src, dest, data?) copies one template file; a .ejs file is rendered with { config, ...data } ctx.copyDir(src, dest, data?, mapPath?) copies a template folder recursi

title: Contributing
text: 1. Write src/recipes/<id .ts with defineRecipe , and its templates in templates/<id / . 2. Register it in src/recipes/registry.ts . 3. Plan it in src/engine/planner.ts : planRecipes for Node, planJava for Java. The order is written by hand; put the recipe after the ones whose files it merges into. 4. If it adds a choice, add the value to src/config/schema.ts , with a cross field rule if some combination cannot work. The schema accepts only what a recipe implements, so a value without a recipe never reaches the planner. 5. Offer it in src/prompts/wizard.ts and in the init options in src/cli.ts

title: Contributing
text: Releases are published from a local machine: prepublishOnly runs the build, the type check and the tests first, and publishConfig makes the package @rsaglobaltech/forja public. There is no release pipeline. The repository contains a .github/workflows/ci.yml , but it is not used: GitHub Actions stay off, and every check above runs locally. Record each change in CHANGELOG.md , and tick the matching box in ROADMAP.md , in the same pull request.

title: Daily use
text: Daily use After forja init , two commands keep working inside the project: forja add writes new pieces of the hexagon in the right place with a passing test, and forja doctor checks that your machine and the project are in shape. Both read forja.config.json . Run them anywhere inside the project; forja walks up the directories until it finds that file. Outside a project you get: forja add The argument is <module /<Name . forja turns the name into PascalCase ( place order and placeOrder both become PlaceOrder ) and the module into lowercase letters and digits ( Order Items becomes orderitems ). On Node, a trailing UseCase is dropped, so PlaceOrderUseCase does not become PlaceOrderUseCaseUseCase . Node Java usecase module required module required entity module optional, and not used in the path module required port module optional, and not used in the path module required Where the files land on Node Everything goes into packages/core . title: End-to-end tests
text: End to end tests tests e2e web adds Playwright to the web app. It tests the app in a real browser, from the home page through sign in, and on Java through the real API. tests replaces the default list, so keep unit,integration in it. In the wizard, Node offers "End to end (Playwright, web)" under Tests, and Java asks "End to end tests of the web app (Playwright)?" after the design system. End to end tests need a web app. Without one, forja refuses: What forja generates All of it lives in apps/web : File Node, auth sessions Node, auth none Java playwright.config.ts yes yes yes e2e/smoke.spec.ts yes yes yes e2e/auth.spec.ts yes no no e2e/tasks.spec.ts no no yes It also adds @playwright/test ~1.63.0 to apps/web , a test:e2e script there, and a root test:e2e that runs it. title: End-to-end tests
text: With the ci extra, the generated .github/workflows/ci.yml gets an e2e job. It sets up Node 22 (and Java 21 with Maven caching on Java), runs docker compose up d wait on Java when the project has PostgreSQL or Keycloak, installs the dependencies, runs npx playwright install with deps chromium and npm run test:e2e , and uploads apps/web/playwright report when a test fails. The ci extra is off by default: it writes a GitHub Actions workflow, which spends Actions minutes on a private repository.

title: The generated project
text: The generated project forja builds a project from recipes. Each recipe writes one concern: the API, the web app, the database, auth, an extra. The configuration decides which recipes run, and in which order. This page goes through them one by one. Run forja init <name yes dry run with your flags to see the exact tree. Node recipes They run in this order: base , shared , core hexagonal , db postgres docker or db none , web , mobile , auth sessions or auth none , mailer console , design tailwind , e2e web , extras lint , ci , specgate . Each one runs only when the configuration asks for it. Recipe Runs when Writes base always root package.json (npm workspaces apps/ , packages/ ; test and typecheck across them), tsconfig.base.json , .gitignore , .editorconfig , README.md , docs/architecture.md , forja.config.json shared always packages/shared : API types and zod validation shared by web and mobile core hexagonal always packages/core : domain, auth use cases, ports, in memory adapters, bcrypt, clock, logger, container.ts , env.ts ; unit tests with unit db postgres docker db: postgres docker docker compose.yml (PostgreSQL 16), drizzle.config.ts , the Drizzle schema and repositories, db:push and db:studio scripts, DATABASE URL db none db: none nothing: the in memory repositories are enough web web in platforms apps/web : Next.js App Router, layout, home page; root dev and build scripts mobile mobile in platforms apps/mobile : Expo Router, app.config.ts , Babel and Metro config; root mobile script; EXPO PUBLIC API URL auth sessions auth: sessions web: login, register, forgot and reset password pages, Server Actions, proxy.ts , a dashboard; with mobile, the /api/auth/ route handlers and the mobile screens; integration tests with integration ; SESSION TTL DAYS auth none auth: none nothing mailer console auth is not none ConsoleMailer and InMemoryMailer in packages/core design tailwind design: tailwind design tokens in packages/shared/src/design ; Tailwind 4 on the web; Nativ

title: The generated project
text: Recipes write to an in memory file system. When all of them have run, forja formats the TypeScript, JavaScript, JSON, CSS and Markdown files with Prettier, and only then writes to disk. A failure part way through leaves nothing behind, and dry run prints that same in memory tree. [Contributing](contributing.md) explains how a recipe is written.

title: Getting started
text: Getting started forja creates a project with a hexagonal core and the apps around it. On the Node path you get a TypeScript monorepo with a Next.js web app and an Expo mobile app. On the Java path you get a Spring Boot or Quarkus API with a Next.js web app as its client. This page walks through the Node path; the [Java backends](java.md) page covers the other one. Requirements Tool When you need it Node.js 22 or newer Always. forja itself and every generated project run on it. npm, pnpm or bun Always. npm is the default; pm picks another on Node. Docker With db postgres docker (the default on Node), for the PostgreSQL in docker compose.yml . JDK 21 Java backends only. Install You can also run it without installing: Your first project, with the wizard The wizard asks for the project name and the backend. For a Node project it then asks for the scope of the internal packages ( @acme/ ), the platforms (web, mobile), the database, authentication, the mailer, the design system, the tests, the extras and the package manager. It only offers what forja can generate, so every answer works. When the files are written, it asks two more questions: install the dependencies now, and initialise git with a first commit. Your first project, with yes yes asks nothing. It takes the defaults and applies any flag you give on top. On Node the defaults are web and mobile, PostgreSQL in Docker, built in sessions, the console mailer, Tailwind, unit and integration tests, and ESLint with Prettier. [Configuration](config.md) lists every default. A web only project with in memory repositories looks like this: With yes , forja installs the dependencies and runs git init without asking. title: Java backends
text: Java backends With backend spring or backend quarkus , forja puts the logic in a Java API in apps/api and makes the Next.js web app a client of that API. The API is hexagonal, with one package per module, and ships with a sample tasks module whose domain and application layers are plain Java. Spring Boot Quarkus Version 4.1.1 3.40.1 Java 21 21 Build Maven Wrapper ( apps/api/mvnw ) Maven Wrapper ( apps/api/mvnw ) Persistence JDBC + Flyway + PostgreSQL JDBC (Agroal) + Flyway + PostgreSQL Real PostgreSQL in tests Testcontainers Dev Services OpenAPI UI /swagger ui.html /q/swagger ui Health /actuator/health /q/health Config file application.yml application.properties Create one The wizard asks the same things in order: the root Java package, ArchUnit, a web app, the database, authentication, the design system, end to end tests and the extras. The Java defaults with yes : a web app, PostgreSQL in Docker, OAuth2 with Keycloak, ArchUnit on, Tailwind, unit and integration tests, and the lint , docker and specgate extras. CI is never on by default; add it with extras lint,docker,specgate,ci if you want a GitHub Actions workflow. The Java package The root package defaults to com.<name , with hyphens removed: forja init my shop gives com.myshop . Choose your own with java package : It must have at least two segments of lowercase letters, digits and underscores. API only Pass an empty platform list and forja skips the web app, packages/shared and the web Dockerfile: Mobile is not available with a Java backend yet; platforms web,mobile is rejected. title: Java backends
text: With auth oauth2 (the default), the pieces fit together like this: The API is an OAuth2 resource server. It validates the JWT and takes the current user from the token's sub , behind the CurrentUser port. Another user's task answers 404. The web app signs in with Auth.js through Authorization Code + PKCE. It keeps the tokens in its encrypted session cookie and calls the API from the server with the access token, so the token never reaches the browser. Sign out is federated. docker compose runs a development Keycloak on http://localhost:8180 that imports infra/keycloak/<name realm.json : a web

title: Java backends
text: Errors come out as RFC 9457 Problem Details ( application/problem+json ) with a stable code , such as task not found . Clients decide on the code , not on the message. OpenAPI and a health endpoint are on from the start.

title: forja and Specgate
text: forja and Specgate [Specgate](https://rsaglobaltech.github.io/specgate/) keeps a project's requirements, their scenarios and the tests that prove them in step. forja can generate a project ready for it, and forja add usecase links each new use case to its requirement. This page covers what forja does; the Specgate documentation covers Specgate itself. Turn it on Specgate comes with the specgate extra. It is on by default for Java backends. On Node, ask for it: In the wizard, tick "Specgate (spec driven development)" under Extras. What forja installs What Where @rsaglobaltech/specgate ^0.19.1 root package.json , devDependencies spec , spec:status , spec:check scripts root package.json , running specgate , specgate status and specgate check The brief to fill in docs/brief.md The day to day guide docs/specgate.md docs/brief.md starts with four fields for Specgate, then a space for the client's brief: Paste the brief below that block as you received it. Specgate checks that every value in a scenario comes from this text or from assumptions.md . Adoption after the install When forja installs the dependencies, it adopts Specgate in the new project: The third line puts the architecture in the gate: specgate check , specgate done and the harness run npm run arch between the specification and the tests, so code in the wrong layer fails the gate even when every test passes. On Node, npm run arch checks the core's import rules; on Java it runs the ArchUnit test alone. It needs Specgate 0.20 or newer; an older one leaves the gate as it was. With git on, it commits the result as chore: adopt Specgate . If you used skip install , or the adoption failed (no network, for example), forja prints those commands among the next steps instead. Either way, the next steps end with: forja doctor warns until the project is adopted, which it detects by the presence of spec.md and docs/specs/traceability.md . title: forja and Specgate
text: The flow below is the one in the generated docs/specgate.md . Run npx specgate on its own whenever you lose track: it shows where the specification stands and the command to run next. 1. Write the brief. Paste the client's brief into docs/brief.md and fill in the four fields. npx specgate draft explains each field; npx specgate draft agent "claude p" lets your agent propose them. 2. Draft a module. Your agent writes the requirements and scenarios, and Specgate checks them against the brief: Without an agent, npx specgate draft orders prints the line to paste into one. Repeat until it says Read

title: forja and Specgate
text: In a project where Specgate is adopted, forja add usecase also creates the requirement: 1. forja checks first that no file would be overwritten, so a refused command leaves no orphan requirement. 2. It runs specgate new "Place order" . The title comes from the class name, or from title . 3. It writes the use case and its test, with the new id in the test's name: On Java, the id goes in @DisplayName("REQ 003 Place order") , and the pending scenario is a @Disabled test. text: Option Effect req REQ 007 names an existing requirement instead of creating one. The id must look like REQ followed by digits. title "Place an order" the title specgate new gets, and the one in the test name no spec no requirement and no id in the test dry run shows the files; creates no requirement req works for requirements that came out of specgate draft : the archived module already has REQ 007 , and you want the code for it.
